text:
ashley: Heads-up — planning to roll out audit schema v4 behind a feature-flag next Tue for Private and Dedicated customers. Need a short customer validation runbook, sample payloads, and a changelog blurb. low-risk rollout but we should be explicit about KMS and RBAC fields.

mike: Quick q — does v4 add any new PII fields or change retention semantics?

ashley: No new PII. Main additions: explicit `rbac_action` and `rbac_resource` (to capture fine-grained allow/deny semantics), `kms_key` metadata object (id, version, key_type), and `trace_id` for cross-service correlation. Retention unchanged.

jen: For KMS, we should ensure we never include the key material — just key metadata (key_id, key_version, provider). Also confirm HSM-backed keys expose limited info. I'll add a short section to the runbook.

ashley: Perfect. Draft runbook sections: 1) purpose + compatibility window, 2) sample payloads, 3) validation steps, 4) customer-facing FAQ blurb, 5) rollback steps.

alex: Suggest a 30-day compatibility window where both v3 and v4 events are emitted and customers can opt into v4 via flag `audit_schema=4`. After 30 days we flip default for new tenants and give 60 days before mandatory.

lia: For Hosted API customers, can we make it opt-in first? Some SOC teams will want a heads-up.

ashley: Yes — hosted will be opt-in initially. Dedicated/Private get the feature-flag rollout described.

kevin: I'll own the changelog entry + release note. Short blurb idea for customers: "Improved audit fidelity: new RBAC action/resource fields and KMS metadata for better forensic correlation. Opt-in for hosted, gradual rollout for dedicated/private." Thoughts?

mike: Add an example of how `rbac_action` maps to existing permissions (e.g., `model.deploy` vs `runtime.invoke`). Customers ask mapping a lot.

ashley: Good call — include mapping table in docs.

security-bot: [automated] schema-validator v2 ran on staging: 12/12 samples passed, 2 warnings about missing `trace_id` in older services.

tariq: On vuln triage: we found a low-severity issue in the audit ingestion path (parsing large arrays). Patch inbound, but it doesn't affect schema itself — will backport to staging.

jen: For customer validation steps, recommend:
1) Pull sample payloads from https://redwood.internal/docs/audit-schema-v4/samples.json
2) Run local validator: `./tools/validate_audit.py --schema v4 sample.json`
3) Verify KMS metadata shows `key_id` only and no secret fields
4) Validate RBAC mappings against your IAM export
5) Confirm log shipping / SIEM parsers still work (we'll provide regex/field mapping)

ashley: I'll add that as the canonical runbook. Can volunteers review the sample payloads and FAQ before EOD Fri?

kevin: I can review FAQ + changelog.

jen: I'll review KMS wording and validation commands.

alex: I'll draft the migration timeline and customer comms draft.

lia: I'll coordinate with solutions-eng to pick 2 pilot customers for early validation.

mike: I'll handle the RBAC mapping doc and include examples showing `allow`/`deny` semantics in audit events.

ashley: Thanks team. Action items: Kevin (changelog + FAQ), Jen (KMS wording + validator), Mike (RBAC mapping), Alex (timeline + comms), Lia (pilot customers). I'll open a GH PR with sample payloads and the runbook link. PR will be linked in the thread.

ashley: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/412 (WIP) :eyes:

security-bot: [automated] created issue #889: "audit-schema-v4 rollout checklist" and assigned to ashley, kevin, jen, mike, alex, lia.

tariq: FYI: I'm scheduling a short incident-runthrough next Wed to ensure ingestion and alerting handle the new fields; it's mostly a smoke test.

ashley: Great — add any alerts that reference field names so we can catch typos.

kevin: Drafted changelog blurb in PR. pinging for quick reviews. :thumbsup:

lia: I'll reach out to the pilot customers with a 1-pager and timeline once the FAQ is ready.

ashley: If no objections, we'll target feature-flag rollout Tue morning and keep it behind opt-in for hosted. Thanks all. :shipit:
